title: Conformal Prediction Sets Quantify Information Gain: A Theoretical Perspective
why_read: A theoretical paper connecting conformal prediction set sizes to information theory, useful for researchers who care about rigorous uncertainty quantification.
analysis: Conformal prediction is a statistical technique that produces prediction sets guaranteed to contain the true answer with a specified probability, and this paper asks what the size of those sets actually tells you about information content. The authors build a generalized entropy framework showing Shannon mutual information can be derived from properties of these prediction sets, and prove relationships like a data processing inequality for this new measure. This is a niche but genuinely rigorous theoretical contribution that formalizes an intuition many practitioners already use informally. It's most relevant to researchers in uncertainty quantification or feature selection rather than general engineers.
